rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. The requirement `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` is only cited, so I did not reassess it.

**Outline of the whole retained file, including when one item is selected**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` selects the second line of a three-item file. It asserts `selected.outline().items.len() == 3`. It also calls `select("")` on the selected content and gets the whole file text back.
- `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected section.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the same pointer equality for a selected function.
- A selected value would fail these checks if it exposed only its own subtree.

**Root first, with an empty selector, covering the entire source**
- The Rust test asserts that `selectors[0]` is `""`.
- It asserts that `items[0].span == Span::new(0, source.len())`.
- The plain-text, Markdown and Unicode tests assert the same root span and selector.
- The empty-file case yields exactly one item, the root, with span `0..0`.
- `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` checks `items[0].selector == ""` and a whole-source span for each bundled language.

**Items in source preorder with full ancestry selectors**
- The Rust test asserts the exact sequence `"" , mod[auth], mod[auth]/fn[check], mod[auth]/struct[Token], fn[last]`. This shows parents before their children, children before later siblings, and ancestry in the selectors. It also asserts the matching kinds.
- The Markdown tests assert nested section selectors such as `section[End]/section[Level%20two]` and `.../block@...`. They also check duplicate `#N` suffixes in source order.
- The plain-text tests assert line items in source order, with the spans and texts of `alpha`, `beta` and `alpha`.
- The Rust and Markdown tests resolve each listed selector back to the matching text with `select`. This shows the selectors identify the items.

No clause of the requirement lacks a test. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} items
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
The root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
